Cross-contract call surface for the yield-adapter (ADR 0006), declared as
a bare trait rather than a dependency on the `yield-adapter` crate.

A Cargo dependency on that crate would also link its `#[contract]`
struct and `#[contractimpl]` block into *this* contract's own compiled
Wasm \xe2\x80\x94 `cdylib` linking includes every reachable Wasm-exported symbol
from any dependency, not just the ones this crate's code actually calls.
That silently duplicated the yield-adapter's entire exported interface
(including a second, incompatible `__constructor`) inside vault-factory's
own binary, breaking function dispatch on both sides. A `#[contractclient]`
trait has no function bodies, so it generates only the thin
address-based call wrapper below and nothing gets exported.

vault-factory never inspects the specific error a yield-adapter call
fails with \xe2\x80\x94 it only ever uses the panicking `Client` methods (`stake`,
`unstake_full`, `unstake_partial`), which abort the whole transaction on
any failure regardless of the concrete e
udt_error_enum_v0.name: YieldAdapterError

function_v0.doc:
FR-2.4/FR-3.1. **Permissionless** \xe2\x80\x94 callable by any address once the
vault's `lock_rule` condition is met. This is the baseline guarantee
that a payout can never be stuck just because Agapay's own keeper
infrastructure is down (see backend/keeper and PRD NFR-2.1).
`triggered_by` is recorded for keeper-incentive accounting (FR-3.2)
but is never authorization-gated.
function_v0.name: release

function_v0.doc:
Swaps this contract's WASM in place, keeping the same contract ID and
all existing storage (vaults, admin, config) intact \xe2\x80\x94 the standard
Soroban upgrade pattern. Without this, any future code change would
require deploying a brand-new contract and losing every vault's
on-chain history, which is far too destructive for a fix or feature
add. Admin-gated, same threshold requirement as every other admin
capability here (FR-2.6).
function_v0.name: upgrade

function_v0.doc: Permissionless maintenance operation used by supervised keepers. It\ncommits TTL extension for the contract instance/code and the selected\npersistent vault entry; unlike read simulation, this changes ledger state.
function_v0.name: extend_ttl

function_v0.doc:
FR-2.3. Any address may fund any vault, not just its owner \xe2\x80\x94 a
deliberately supported use case, not an edge case to block.

ADR 0006: vaults always stake \xe2\x80\x94 this is not an opt-in path, so
fund_vault requires a configured yield-adapter and immediately
delegates the received amount to it. `pool_id` is an off-chain
"best current yield" hint (see backend/api/src/yield/blendRates.ts)
\xe2\x80\x94 the yield-adapter contract still executes the actual token
movement, so a wrong hint can only mean a worse pool, never a way to
misdirect funds (same reasoning as `release`'s `triggered_by`).
function_v0.name: fund_vault

function_v0.doc:
Emergency stop on *new* vault activity only. Never gates `release()`
\xe2\x80\x94 pausing the ability to pay out already-funded vaults would defeat
the FR-3.1/NFR-2.1 "money never gets stuck" guarantee this whole
design exists to provide.
function_v0.name: set_paused

function_v0.doc:
Lets an owner walk away from a vault that never received any
funding. Deliberately unavailable once even one atomic unit is funded \xe2\x80\x94
real money in the vault means release() is the only safe exit
(FR-3.1's "money never gets stuck" guarantee), never a cancel path.
function_v0.name: cancel_vault

function_v0.doc:
FR-2.1/FR-2.2. Requires `owner.require_auth()` \xe2\x80\x94 creating a vault is
not permissionless (unlike `release`, see FR-3.1).

`Schedule`/`Pct` are now accepted alongside `Manual` (drip release) \xe2\x80\x94
see `release()`'s per-rule branch for how each pays out.
function_v0.name: create_vault

function_v0.doc:
Backstop for a vault whose stored `split_rule` can never be satisfied
by `release()` \xe2\x80\x94 e.g. a `Percentage` split that doesn't sum to
10,000 bps, created before `validate_split` caught this at creation
time (the exact bug class behind a real stuck testnet vault). This is
deliberately *not* a general admin override \xe2\x80\x94 every guard below
exists so a compromised or malicious admin key still can't use this
to redirect funds anywhere but the vault's own beneficiaries:

- Only fires when `split_amounts` \xe2\x80\x94 the identical computation
`release()` itself would run \xe2\x80\x94 provably fails on this vault's own
stored data, re-derived here rather than taken on the caller's
word. A vault `release()` could actually complete is never
eligible, so this can never be used to shortcut a normal release
or skip its own conditions (due date, target-met, schedule).
- No destination parameter. Funds always go to the vault's own
already-stored beneficiaries, split evenly \xe2\x80\x94 the broken
split_rule's own numbers are exactly what can't be tr
function_v0.name: rescue_vault

function_v0.doc:
One-time setup. `admin` should itself be a Stellar multisig (M-of-N)
account, not a single key \xe2\x80\x94 see FR-2.6 and ADR 0001's note that
Stellar's native multisig satisfies this requirement directly.

This is a Soroban constructor (Protocol 22+), not a regular
`initialize` function called in a second transaction after deploy.
That distinction is load-bearing: a constructor runs atomically as
part of the `CreateContractV2` host operation, in the *same*
transaction that deploys the contract (`stellar contract deploy
--wasm ... -- --admin <address>`), and the host only ever invokes it
from that internal path \xe2\x80\x94 no transaction submitted after deployment
can call `__constructor` again, at any address, by anyone (see
`call_constructor` in soroban-env-host, which runs it with
`internal_host_call: true`, unreachable from `invoke_contract`).

function_v0.doc: Assigns the Agapay fee recipient. Production deployments should set\nthis to a separately controlled treasury rather than an operator key.
function_v0.name: set_fee_treasury

function_v0.doc:
Adds or removes an asset from the set `create_vault` may denominate
a vault in \xe2\x80\x94 mirrors yield-adapter's Blend pool allowlist
(`set_pool_allowed`). Without this, any syntactically-valid contract
address could be named as `asset`, including one an attacker
controls with adversarial `transfer()` logic, with no on-chain
restriction to real, vetted stablecoins (the PRD's own "stablecoins
only" requirement was previously enforced nowhere on-chain).
function_v0.name: set_asset_allowed

function_v0.doc: Configures the yield-adapter contract fund_vault/release delegate\nstaking to (ADR 0006). Admin-gated, same threshold requirement as\nevery other admin capability here (FR-2.6).
function_v0.name: set_yield_adapter

fields.doc: Denomination asset's Stellar Asset Contract address. Stablecoins only (PRD B.2.5).
fields.name: asset

fields.doc: Principal required to satisfy target-based locks: target + fee.
fields.name: funding_target

fields.doc:
The next timestamp a `Schedule`/`Pct` drip interval becomes due.
Starts at `due_date`, advances by `interval_seconds` after each
non-final drip. Unused by `Manual` (its own `due_date` check via
`lock_rule` is what gates it).
fields.name: next_release_at

fields.doc: Agapay protocol fee fixed at creation from target and duration.
fields.name: platform_fee

fields.doc:
Reentrancy guard. Set true immediately before `release()`/
`rescue_vault()` call out to the yield-adapter (and, transitively,
Blend) \xe2\x80\x94 both functions need that call's *return value* to compute
the final balance/status, so the usual "write final state before any
external call" ordering isn't available here. This flag is the
fallback: it closes the window a reentrant call could otherwise walk
through while this vault's real final state is still unwritten. Not
currently known to be exploitable (neither SEP-41 token transfers nor
Blend's `pool.submit()` call back into arbitrary caller contracts),
but that's an assumption about every current *and future* allowlisted
asset/pool, not a structural guarantee \xe2\x80\x94 found in an adversarial
security review ahead of mainnet.
fields.name: releasing

fields.doc:
Snapshotted from the contract's global `yield_adapter` the moment this
vault is first funded \xe2\x80\x94 never re-read afterward, even if admin later
calls `set_yield_adapter` to point new vaults elsewhere. Without this,
an admin changing the global adapter while this vault still has an
open position there orphans it permanently: both `release()` and its
own `rescue_vault()` backstop would call the *new* adapter, which has
no record of this vault's position (`PositionNotFound`), with no
path back to the old adapter either. `None` until first funded.
fields.name: yield_adapter

udt_union_v0.doc:
What condition gates `release()`, independent of `ReleaseRule`'s payout
*shape*. Mirrors the vocabulary the wizard already shows users
(frontend/web/src/vaultWizard.ts's `LockRule`) \xe2\x80\x94 previously collected
from users but never actually enforced on-chain; `release()` checked
`due_date` unconditionally regardless of what a user picked. FR-2.4
requires a target-gated rule to actually revert if the target isn't met.
udt_union_v0.name: LockRule

void_v0.doc: Gated on `due_date` only \xe2\x80\x94 today's only enforced behavior.
void_v0.name: TargetDate

void_v0.doc: Gated on `current_balance >= funding_target` only, no date requirement.
void_v0.name: TargetMet

void_v0.doc: No additional gate beyond the vault being `Active`.
void_v0.name: None

udt_union_v0.doc: How a release is divided among beneficiaries. Mirrors cal-core's `SplitRule`.
udt_union_v0.name: SplitRule

tuple_v0.doc: Beneficiary index -> principal amount at the vault target. Values must\nbe positive and sum to `target_amount`; yield/shortfall scales them\nproportionally, with final-beneficiary rounding dust.

tuple_v0.doc: Beneficiary index -> percentage (parts per 10_000, i.e. basis points).

void_v0.name: Manual

void_v0.doc:
Owner-cancelled while still unfunded (`current_balance == 0`) \xe2\x80\x94 a
terminal state, same as Completed/Archived. Never reachable once any
funding has landed, since real money means release() is the only
safe way out (FR-3.1's "money never gets stuck" guarantee).
void_v0.name: Cancelled

udt_struct_v0.doc: Emitted on every successful `release()` call. Indexed by Mercury (ADR 0003)\ninto the off-chain `ReleaseEvent` cache \xe2\x80\x94 this on-chain event is the source\nof truth (NFR-4.2), the indexed copy is a derived, rebuildable cache.
udt_struct_v0.name: ReleaseEvent

fields.doc: Parallel to `Vault.beneficiaries` \xe2\x80\x94 amounts[i] paid to beneficiaries[i].
fields.name: amounts

udt_struct_v0.doc:
`#[contracttype]` enums only support unit variants or single-value tuple
variants (soroban-sdk 27 rejects multi-field struct variants at the
TryFromVal level) \xe2\x80\x94 so `Schedule`/`Pct` each wrap a dedicated params
struct rather than carrying two named fields directly.
udt_struct_v0.name: ScheduleParams

fields.doc: Day of the calendar month (1-28) a drip may land on. 28 is the cap\nso every month has that day, avoiding February edge cases. 0 = not\nused. Mutually exclusive with `days_of_week`.
fields.name: day_of_month

fields.doc:
Bitmask of allowed weekdays a drip may land on: bit 0 = Sunday ...
bit 6 = Saturday (same convention as JS `Date.getUTCDay()`, so the
wizard's day-of-week picker maps directly). 0 = not used. Mutually
exclusive with `day_of_month`.
fields.name: days_of_week

fields.doc:
Flat step in seconds between drips. Only used when both fields below
are 0 \xe2\x80\x94 a calendar-anchored schedule (weekday or day-of-month)
overrides it, since "every N seconds" can't express "every Monday"
or "the 15th of the month" (months/weeks aren't a fixed number of
seconds). See `next_schedule_release` in lib.rs.
fields.name: interval_seconds

udt_struct_v0.doc: Emitted after funds have been transferred and successfully supplied to the\napproved yield pool. This is the durable source for funding reconciliation.
udt_struct_v0.name: VaultFundedEvent

udt_struct_v0.doc: Emitted when a vault is created so off-chain views can discover the new\nidentifier without scanning contract storage.
udt_struct_v0.name: VaultCreatedEvent

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Emitted by `rescue_vault` \xe2\x80\x94 deliberately a distinct event from
`VaultReleased`, never reused, so a rescue is always visible on-chain as
exactly what it is: a backstop path taken because the vault's stored
split_rule could never satisfy a normal `release()`, not a normal payout.
udt_struct_v0.name: VaultRescuedEvent

fields.doc: Equal split among the vault's own stored beneficiaries \xe2\x80\x94 rescue never\ntakes a caller-supplied distribution, only this one deterministic\nfallback, precisely so the admin has no discretion over amounts.
fields.name: amounts

udt_struct_v0.doc: Emitted when an owner cancels their own still-unfunded vault.
udt_struct_v0.name: VaultCancelledEvent
